papers.title: Energy deposition in planetary and exoplanetary atmospheres induced by cosmic rays
papers.abstract: Cosmic rays can significantly alter the abundances of certain species in the upper layers of planetary atmospheres, especially in terms of their biosignatures. To fully understand the extent of this effect, it is essential to accurately model the interactions of cosmic rays with planetary magnetic fields. We used the CosmicTransmutation code to study the effect of a planetary magnetic field on the flux of galactic cosmic rays and stellar energetic particles. We found that both particle sources are significantly affected by magnetic fields, even though the effects are different due to the varying energy ranges that characterize each source. The stellar energetic particle energy flux is significantly higher for an Earth-like planet with no magnetic field, but with a magnetic field of 30\,μT or higher, the energy flux of the two sources becomes comparable. We find that the atmospheric pressures the cosmic rays reach are significantly lower than those found in previous studies using simpler models and that the effect of the atmospheric composition on this outcome is small. We found similar results using the model for the exoplanet K2-18b, even though the radius is significantly larger than Earth's. Because the two cosmic ray sources cover different energy ranges and are affected by the magnetic field in different ways as a result, both sources should be considered. Future studies should focus on combining an accurate modelling procedure of the interaction between cosmic rays and planetary magnetic fields with atmospheric chemistry models. This will require general circulation models to capture the latitudinal and longitudinal dependencies in full.
papers.summary:
**Why It Matters**
Space is full of fast-moving particles called cosmic rays. Some come from far outside our solar system, and others are flung out by a planet's own star during outbursts. When they slam into the top of a planet's atmosphere, they can change which gases are present. That matters especially for "biosignatures," the chemical fingerprints that astronomers hope will reveal life on distant worlds. If cosmic rays quietly alter those fingerprints, we could misread what we see. A planet's magnetic field acts like an invisible umbrella, steering many of these particles away, so any realistic estimate has to account for it.

**What They Did**
The researchers used a computer program called CosmicTransmutation to simulate how two kinds of particles, galactic cosmic rays and stellar energetic particles, behave around a planet with a magnetic field. They tested an Earth-like planet and also K2-18b, an exoplanet much larger than Earth. They also varied the magnetic field strength and the makeup of the atmosphere.

**Key Findings**
Magnetic fields strongly affect both particle sources, but in different ways, because the two sources carry different amounts of energy. For an Earth-like planet with no magnetic field, the star's particles deliver much more energy. With a field of 30 microtesla or higher, the two sources deliver comparable amounts. The particles also reach much thinner, higher parts of the atmosphere than earlier, simpler models predicted, and the atmosphere's composition has only a small effect on this. K2-18b gave similar results despite its much larger radius.

**Looking Forward**
Because the two sources act differently, future studies should include both. The authors recommend pairing this detailed treatment of cosmic rays and magnetic fields with atmospheric chemistry models. Capturing how the effects vary across a planet's latitudes and longitudes will require general circulation models, which are 3D computer simulations of a planet's atmosphere.

papers.title_tr: Kozmik ışınların neden olduğu gezegen ve ötegezegen atmosferlerinde enerji birikimi
papers.summary_tr:
**Neden Önemli**
Uzay, kozmik ışın adı verilen çok hızlı parçacıklarla dolu. Bunların bir kısmı Güneş Sistemi'nin çok dışından gelir, bir kısmı ise gezegenin kendi yıldızının patlamalarıyla fırlatılır. Bu parçacıklar bir gezegenin atmosferinin üst katmanına çarptığında, orada hangi gazların bulunduğunu değiştirebilir. Bu durum, uzak dünyalarda yaşam izi aramak için kullanılan kimyasal parmak izleri olan "biyoimzalar" açısından özellikle önemlidir. Kozmik ışınlar bu parmak izlerini sessizce değiştiriyorsa, gözlediklerimizi yanlış yorumlayabiliriz. Gezegenin manyetik alanı görünmez bir şemsiye gibi çalışır ve bu parçacıkların çoğunu yönlendirip uzaklaştırır. Bu yüzden gerçekçi her tahminde manyetik alan hesaba katılmalıdır.

**Ne Yaptılar**
Araştırmacılar, CosmicTransmutation adlı bir bilgisayar programıyla iki tür parçacığın, yani galaktik kozmik ışınların ve yıldız kaynaklı enerjik parçacıkların, manyetik alanı olan bir gezegenin çevresinde nasıl davrandığını simüle etti. Dünya benzeri bir gezegeni ve Dünya'dan çok daha büyük bir ötegezegen olan K2-18b'yi test ettiler. Ayrıca manyetik alanın şiddetini ve atmosferin bileşimini değiştirdiler.

**Ana Bulgular**
Manyetik alanlar her iki parçacık kaynağını da güçlü biçimde etkiler, ancak iki kaynağın taşıdığı enerji farklı olduğu için etkiler birbirinden farklıdır. Manyetik alanı olmayan Dünya benzeri bir gezegende yıldızdan gelen parçacıklar çok daha fazla enerji taşır. 30 mikrotesla veya daha yüksek bir alanda ise iki kaynağın taşıdığı enerji birbirine yakın hale gelir. Parçacıklar, önceki basit modellerin öngördüğünden çok daha ince ve yüksek atmosfer katmanlarına ulaşır; atmosferin bileşiminin bu sonuca etkisi ise küçüktür. K2-18b için de yarıçapı çok daha büyük olmasına rağmen benzer sonuçlar elde edildi.

**İleriye Bakış**
İki kaynak farklı davrandığı için gelecekteki çalışmalarda ikisi de dikkate alınmalıdır. Yazarlar, kozmik ışınların ve manyetik alanların bu ayrıntılı modellemesinin atmosfer kimyası modelleriyle birleştirilmesini öneriyor. Etkilerin gezegenin enlemlerine ve boylamlarına göre nasıl değiştiğini tam olarak yakalamak için, gezegen atmosferinin üç boyutlu bilgisayar simülasyonları olan genel dolaşım modelleri gerekecek.

papers.title: The Dyn-Atmo Survey: High-contrast Imaging Spectroscopy of the Substellar Companion HD 13724 B with the JWST NIRSpec IFU
papers.abstract: We present the first spectral analysis from the JWST Cycle 3 GO Program #6362, the Dyn-Atmo Survey of dynamical-atmospheric benchmarks, characterizing the atmospheres of directly-imaged companions with dynamical masses and measured orbits. This program has obtained moderate-resolution spectra (R 2700, 3-5μm) using the NIRSpec/G395H IFU. We observe the T4-dwarf companion, HD 13724 B, companion to a G-type star at a projected angular separation of 0''2. Updated orbital monitoring constrains the mass to 38.3±0.6 MJuₚ, which we use as a Gaussian prior when inferring the atmospheric state. We fit the continuum-subtracted spectrum using the BT-SETTL, Sonora Diamondback, Sonora Flame Skimmer, and NEWERA-PHOENIX self-consistent model grids, together with petitRADTRANS atmospheric retrievals. We adopt bulk parameter values of T_eff=1150±195 K, g=5.1±0.3 dex, [M/H]=0.4±0.4, ₁₀(Kzz)=6.33₋₂.₂₂⁺².⁵⁹, and C/O=0.50±0.13 using a bayesian average across model grids. We find degeneracies in the models between surface gravity, metallicity, and Kzz for Sonora Diamondback and Flame Skimmer. The Flame Skimmer and NEWERA-PHOENIX vertical mixing strengths are incompatible, with Flame Skimmer finding a systematically lower value. The retrievals favor an atmosphere in chemical equilibrium, with enhanced metallicity and a solar C/O ratio, but with no detection of disequilibrium chemistry, and no detection of trace gases other than CH₄, CO₂, ¹²CO and H₂O. Ultimately, we identify critical challenges in forward modeling continuum-subtracted G395H spectra in the low signal-to-noise regime. We find that including independent dynamical mass measurements better constrains atmospheric parameters, but degeneracies between self-consistent model parameters limit accurate atmospheric parameter inferences.
papers.summary:
**Why It Matters**
Astronomers can learn a lot about a distant object's atmosphere from its light, but only if they trust the computer models used to read that light. HD 13724 B is a good test case. It is a "brown dwarf," an object heavier than a giant planet but too light to shine as a true star. It orbits a Sun-like star, and its mass is known from watching its orbit. That makes it a benchmark, a bit like a math problem whose answer is already in the back of the book. Checking the models against it shows whether they can be trusted for similar objects.

**What They Did**
The team used the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) and its NIRSpec instrument to split the object's infrared light (3–5 microns) into fine detail. The companion sits very close to its star, only 0.2 arcseconds away, so separating the two was hard. Orbital tracking gave the companion's mass as 38.3 ± 0.6 times Jupiter's. The team fed that mass into four widely used families of atmosphere models, plus a different method called a retrieval, which works out the atmosphere's ingredients directly from the data.

**Key Findings**
Averaged across the models, the companion has a temperature of about 1150 K (±195 K), a metal-rich atmosphere, and a carbon-to-oxygen ratio of about 0.50, similar to the Sun's. The retrievals found methane, carbon dioxide, carbon monoxide and water, and no other gases. They found no sign of the churning, out-of-balance chemistry that vertical mixing can cause. Several model settings (gravity, metal content and mixing strength) could trade off against each other and give similar fits. Two model families also disagreed on how strong the vertical mixing is. Using the known mass tightened the results, but these overlaps still limit how precise the answers can be.

**Looking Forward**
The authors point to real difficulties in modeling this kind of data when the signal is faint. This is the first result from a larger JWST survey of similar benchmark companions, which should show whether the model disagreements are common and help improve the models.

papers.title_tr: Dyn-Atmo Araştırması: HD 13724 B Yıldız Altı Eşinin JWST NIRSpec IFU ile Yüksek Kontrastlı Görüntüleme Tayfölçümü
papers.summary_tr:
**Neden Önemli**
Gökbilimciler uzak bir cismin atmosferi hakkında çok şey öğrenebilir, ancak bunun için ışığı yorumlayan bilgisayar modellerine güvenmeleri gerekir. HD 13724 B iyi bir test nesnesidir. Bu cisim "kahverengi cüce"dir: dev bir gezegenden daha ağır, ama gerçek bir yıldız gibi parlayamayacak kadar hafiftir. Güneş benzeri bir yıldızın çevresinde dolanır ve kütlesi yörüngesinin izlenmesiyle bilinir. Bu yüzden bir ölçüt (kıyaslama) nesnesidir; cevabı kitabın arkasında yazılı bir matematik problemi gibi düşünülebilir. Modelleri bu nesneyle sınamak, benzer cisimler için ne kadar güvenilir olduklarını gösterir.

**Ne Yaptılar**
Ekip, James Webb Uzay Teleskobu (JWST) ve NIRSpec cihazıyla nesnenin kızılötesi ışığını (3–5 mikron) ince ayrıntılarına ayırdı. Eş, yıldızına yalnızca 0,2 yay saniyesi uzaklıkta olduğundan ikisini birbirinden ayırmak zordu. Yörünge takibi, eşin kütlesini Jüpiter'in 38,3 ± 0,6 katı olarak verdi. Ekip bu kütleyi, yaygın kullanılan dört atmosfer modeli ailesine girdi. Ayrıca atmosferin bileşenlerini doğrudan veriden çıkaran "geri çatım" (retrieval) yöntemini de kullandı.

**Ana Bulgular**
Modellerin ortalamasına göre eşin sıcaklığı yaklaşık 1150 K (±195 K), atmosferi metalce zengin ve karbon/oksijen oranı Güneş'inkine benzer biçimde yaklaşık 0,50'dir. Geri çatım yöntemi metan, karbondioksit, karbonmonoksit ve su buldu; başka gaz bulamadı. Dikey karışımın yol açabileceği dengeden uzak kimyaya dair bir işaret de görülmedi. Bazı model ayarları (yerçekimi, metal miktarı ve karışım şiddeti) birbirinin yerini tutarak benzer uyumlar verebiliyordu. İki model ailesi de dikey karışımın şiddeti konusunda çelişti. Bilinen kütleyi kullanmak sonuçları daraltsa da bu örtüşmeler kesinliği hâlâ sınırlıyor.

**İleriye Bakış**
Yazarlar, sinyal zayıf olduğunda bu tür verileri modellemenin gerçek zorluklar taşıdığına dikkat çekiyor. Bu çalışma, benzer ölçüt eşlerini inceleyen daha geniş bir JWST taramasının ilk sonucudur. Tarama, model uyuşmazlıklarının yaygın olup olmadığını gösterebilir ve modellerin geliştirilmesine yardımcı olabilir.

papers.title: WASP-43b TESS Phase Curve Mapping: Evidence for a Hot Interior
papers.abstract: Phase-curve mapping probes various atmospheric properties depending on wavelength: thermal phase curves are dominated by atmospheric emission, while visible and near-infrared phase curves include reflected light. The measured planetary phase curve offset--the longitudinal offset of the hemisphere of peak brightness from the substellar point--is therefore sensitive to differing atmospheric processes in emission-dominated vs. reflection-dominated bands. In particular, planets with partial western-dayside reflective cloud coverage show a westward reflected-light phase-curve offset relative to the thermal wavelengths. In this work, we analyze five sectors of TESS phase curve observations of the hot Jupiter WASP-43b and compare to previous published multi-band analyses to investigate dayside cloud coverage. We measure a mid-eclipse depth of 130 ± 34 ppm, indicating excess TESS planetary brightness above expectations based on observed and modeled thermal emission. Attributing this excess flux to reflection, we estimate a low geometric albedo of Ag ≈ 0.05 - 0.10. These findings support previous conclusions that WASP-43b lacks any significant cloud coverage on its dayside. Phase-curve mapping reveals a large eastward phase curve offset of 44 ± 18 degrees, significantly eastward of offsets measured at longer wavelengths with JWST, providing evidence for a cloud-free dayside. Both the detection of excess emission in the TESS band and the large measured eastward phase-curve offset support the conclusion that WASP-43b has a hot deep atmosphere that is probed at short wavelengths.
papers.summary:
**Why It Matters**
WASP-43b is a "hot Jupiter," a giant gas planet that orbits so close to its star that one side is always bathed in daylight while the other stays in darkness. Whether clouds cover the daytime side changes how the planet reflects starlight and how heat moves around it. Figuring out whether a faraway world has clear or cloudy skies is a step toward understanding weather on planets far beyond our solar system.

**What They Did**
The team studied five sectors (observing stretches) of data from TESS, the Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite. They built a "phase curve," which tracks the combined brightness of the star and planet as the planet circles its star. It works like watching the Moon's phases: we see the planet's day side and night side in turn. They measured how deeply the light dips when the planet slips behind its star, and how far the brightest spot is shifted from the point directly beneath the star. Visible light includes reflected starlight, so clouds on the western part of the dayside would push the brightest spot westward. The team compared their results with earlier studies at other wavelengths, including those from the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST).

**Key Findings**
The dip when the planet hides behind its star was 130 ± 34 parts per million, more brightness than the planet's heat glow alone would predict. Assuming the extra light is reflected starlight, the planet's reflectivity (geometric albedo) is low, about 0.05 to 0.10. In other words, the planet is quite dark. The brightest spot sits 44 ± 18 degrees east of the point under the star, farther east than JWST measured at longer wavelengths. Both results point to a dayside without significant clouds. They also suggest a hot, deep atmosphere that shows through at the shorter wavelengths TESS sees.

**Looking Forward**
This work shows that comparing a planet's brightness patterns at different wavelengths can reveal whether clouds are present. Differences in the brightest spot's position from one color of light to another act as a clue. The result supports earlier conclusions that WASP-43b's dayside is cloud-free, and it adds a new line of evidence about the planet's hot, deep atmosphere.

The dip when the planet hides behind its star was 130 ± 34 parts per million, more brightness than the planet's heat glow alone would predict. The brightest spot sits 44 ± 18 degrees east of the point under the star, farther east than JWST measured at longer wavelengths. Both results point to a dayside without significant clouds. They also suggest a hot, deep atmosphere that shows through at the shorter wavelengths TESS sees.

This work shows that comparing a planet's brightness patterns at different wavelengths can reveal whether clouds are present. Differences in the brightest spot's position from one color of light to another act as a clue. The result supports earlier conclusions that WASP-43b's dayside is cloud-free, and it adds a new line of evidence about the planet's hot, deep atmosphere.

papers.title: The Dyn-Atmo Survey: JWST/NIRSpec spectroscopy of dynamical benchmark GJ 758 B
papers.abstract: We present new JWST/NIRSpec IFU high contrast spectroscopic observations of the brown dwarf companion GJ 758 B. Extensive radial velocity monitoring of the primary has enabled high-precision measurements of the companion mass through characterization of their joint orbital dynamics. The combination of prior space- and ground-based photometry and spectroscopic observations in concert with a spectral model-independent mass makes this target an ideal benchmark for calibrating evolutionary models with known mass-age-luminosity degeneracies. A template-matching analysis on the NIRSpec/IFU data (F290LP,G395H; λ [2.87-5.27] μm) detects the companion at the expected orbital position with incredible significance (265.2σ). Comprehensive spectral analysis including published datasets over a variety of different spectral model families reveal that an inference using a uniform radius prior is plagued by inaccurate posteriors. The atmospheric model degeneracy between metallicity, gravity, and clouds pull the inferred mass/gravity/radius to an unphysical portion of parameter space for all model families tested. A constrained inference with a gaussian prior on the mass can mitigate this issue but models without clouds still struggle to accurately reproduce the K-band photometry and result in mass inferences which are inconsistent with the dynamics. We explore modifying the spectral models with custom post-processed clouds and molecular abundance perturbations of ammonia and hydrogen sulfide. We find the best-fitting model includes clouds with no patchiness (hole fraction f_hole = 0), a small fractional depletion in ammonia and moderate enhancement in hydrogen sulfide.
papers.summary:
**Why It Matters**
Brown dwarfs are "failed stars": objects too heavy to be planets but too light to ignite like the Sun. Their atmospheres resemble those of giant planets, so they are useful stand-ins for studying distant worlds. To read their light correctly, though, astronomers depend on computer models of how these objects cool and age. Those models need to be tested against cases where the true answer is already known. GJ 758 B is one such case. Its mass was measured directly from the gravitational tug it exerts on its host star, GJ 758, which was tracked over many years. That makes it a rare "answer key" for checking whether our models are honest.

**What They Did**
The team used the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) and its NIRSpec instrument to split the faint companion's light into a spectrum covering wavelengths from 2.87 to 5.27 micrometers. They combined it with older space- and ground-based measurements. They then fitted several families of atmosphere models to see which properties (mass, gravity, size, metallicity, clouds) best matched the light. Finally, they modified the models by hand, adjusting the clouds and the amounts of ammonia and hydrogen sulfide gas.

**Key Findings**
The companion was detected at its expected position with extremely high statistical significance (265.2σ). When the models were left free to choose the object's size, they drifted toward physically unrealistic answers for every model family. This happened because metallicity, gravity and clouds can mimic one another in the spectrum. Fixing the mass to the dynamical value helped. Even so, models without clouds struggled to reproduce the K-band brightness (a near-infrared colour range) and gave masses that disagreed with the dynamical one. The best-fitting model had uniform clouds with no gaps, a slight shortage of ammonia and a moderate excess of hydrogen sulfide.

**Looking Forward**
The results show that current models of brown dwarf atmospheres need better treatment of clouds and chemistry. Using objects with independently known masses, such as GJ 758 B, should help fix these problems. That would make future measurements of brown dwarfs and giant exoplanets more trustworthy.

papers.title_tr: Dyn-Atmo Araştırması: Dinamik Referans Nesnesi GJ 758 B'nin JWST/NIRSpec Tayf Gözlemleri
papers.summary_tr:
**Neden Önemli**
Kahverengi cüceler, "başarısız yıldızlar" olarak bilinir: gezegen olmak için fazla ağır, Güneş gibi nükleer füzyonu başlatmak için ise fazla hafiftirler. Atmosferleri devasa gezegenlerinkine benzediği için uzak dünyaları incelemede işe yarayan birer vekil görevi görürler. Ancak bu nesnelerin ışığını doğru yorumlamak için gökbilimciler, nesnelerin nasıl soğuyup yaşlandığını anlatan bilgisayar modellerine güvenir. Bu modellerin, doğru cevabın önceden bilindiği örneklerle sınanması gerekir. GJ 758 B böyle bir örnektir. Kütlesi, ana yıldızı GJ 758 üzerinde yarattığı kütleçekimsel etkinin yıllarca izlenmesiyle doğrudan ölçülmüştür. Bu da onu modellerin dürüstlüğünü denetlemek için nadir bir "cevap anahtarı" yapar.

**Ne Yaptılar**
Ekip, James Webb Uzay Teleskobu (JWST) ve NIRSpec cihazıyla bu sönük eşlikçinin ışığını 2,87 ile 5,27 mikrometre arasındaki dalga boylarını kapsayan bir tayfa ayırdı. Bunu daha eski uzay ve yer tabanlı ölçümlerle birleştirdi. Ardından kütle, yüzey çekimi, boyut, metal bolluğu ve bulutlar gibi özelliklerden hangilerinin ışığa en iyi uyduğunu görmek için birkaç atmosfer modeli ailesini veriye uydurdu. Son olarak modelleri elle değiştirerek bulutları, amonyak ve hidrojen sülfür gazlarının miktarlarını ayarladı.

**Ana Bulgular**
Eşlikçi, beklenen konumunda son derece yüksek bir istatistiksel anlamlılıkla (265,2σ) tespit edildi. Modellerin nesnenin boyutunu serbestçe seçmesine izin verildiğinde, her model ailesi fiziksel olarak gerçekçi olmayan sonuçlara kaydı. Bunun nedeni, metal bolluğu, yüzey çekimi ve bulutların tayfta birbirini taklit edebilmesidir. Kütleyi dinamik değere sabitlemek yardımcı oldu. Buna rağmen bulutsuz modeller K bandındaki parlaklığı (yakın kızılötesinde bir renk aralığı) yeniden üretmekte zorlandı ve dinamik kütleyle uyuşmayan kütleler verdi. En iyi uyum, boşluksuz ve düzgün bulutlara, amonyakta hafif bir eksikliğe ve hidrojen sülfürde orta düzeyde bir fazlalığa sahip modelle elde edildi.

**İleriye Bakış**
Sonuçlar, kahverengi cüce atmosfer modellerinin bulutları ve kimyayı daha iyi ele alması gerektiğini gösteriyor. GJ 758 B gibi kütlesi bağımsız olarak bilinen nesneler bu sorunların giderilmesine yardımcı olabilir. Bu da kahverengi cücelerin ve devasa ötegezegenlerin gelecekteki ölçümlerini daha güvenilir kılacaktır.

papers.title: Constraining Tidal Migration with the Hot Jupiter Population
papers.abstract: Hot Jupiters with orbital periods shorter than a few days have probably been affected by tidal orbital migration. We develop an analytical framework for constraining tidal migration from the present-day hot Jupiter period distribution, taking into account the uncertain rate and period distribution of hot Jupiters produced by mechanisms such as high-eccentricity migration or disk-driven migration. Assuming the tidal migration timescale is proportional to Pχ_τ, solutions with χ_τ eq 3, 1.7, and 5.6 are all compatible with the present-day period distribution. The χ_τ eq 3 solution is consistent with equilibrium tides with suppression of dissipation at short periods, and implies that newly circularized hot Jupiters have periods concentrated near 3-4 days, as predicted in some high-eccentricity migration models. The χ_τ eq 1.7 solution is also compatible with the 3-4 day peak but has no clear counterpart in existing tidal theories and is more finely tuned. The χ_τ eq 5.6 solution is compatible with enhanced short-period equilibrium tidal dissipation or weakly nonlinear gravity-wave dissipation, but requires circularization at unexpectedly short periods. Thus, we find the model with χ_τ eq 3 most appealing. Transit timing of individual systems and observational constraints on the rate of hot Jupiter engulfment provide additional constraints, which are presently inconclusive but should improve with future data. Improved measurements of the occurrence of short-period planets as a function of planet mass and system age could also help to sharpen the constraints on tidal migration.
papers.summary:
**Why It Matters**
Hot Jupiters are giant planets that circle their stars in just a few days, much closer than Mercury is to our Sun. They probably did not form there. They most likely began farther out and moved inward. Once a planet is that close, tides come into play. These are the same kind of gravitational stretching that the Moon causes in Earth's oceans. Over time, tides can pull a planet's orbit tighter and tighter. How strongly tides act inside giant planets is poorly understood, and that uncertainty limits our picture of how these planets live and die.

**What They Did**
The researchers built a mathematical framework that works backward from the orbital periods of hot Jupiters we see today. It allows for the fact that we don't know how many hot Jupiters were originally made, or at what orbital periods they first settled. Two main routes could have produced them. In high-eccentricity migration, a planet is flung onto a stretched-out orbit and later rounded off. In disk-driven migration, a planet slides inward through the gas disk around a young star. The team assumed the time tides need to shrink an orbit grows with the orbital period raised to a power, called χ_τ, and tested which values of that power fit the data.

**Key Findings**
Three values of χ_τ (3, 1.7, and 5.6) all match the observed period distribution. The authors favor χ_τ = 3. It fits equilibrium tides, the simplest kind of tidal flexing, with weaker energy loss at short periods. It also implies that newly circularized hot Jupiters start out with periods concentrated around 3–4 days, as some high-eccentricity migration models predict. The 1.7 solution also fits that 3–4 day peak, but no existing tidal theory explains it and it needs more fine-tuning. The 5.6 solution could be explained by enhanced tidal dissipation at short periods or by weakly nonlinear gravity waves inside the planet. However, it requires planets to circularize at unexpectedly short periods.

**Looking Forward**
Two other kinds of evidence could narrow the options but are not conclusive yet. One is transit timing, which tracks tiny changes in the orbit of individual planets. The other is how often stars swallow their hot Jupiters. Better measurements of how common short-period planets are, split by planet mass and by the age of the system, could also sharpen the answer.

Araştırmacılar, bugün gözlemlediğimiz sıcak Jüpiterlerin yörünge dönemlerinden geriye doğru giden matematiksel bir çerçeve geliştirdiler. Ayrıca bazı yüksek dış merkezlikli göç modellerinin öngördüğü gibi, yörüngesi yeni yuvarlaklaşmış sıcak Jüpiterlerin dönemlerinin 3–4 gün civarında yoğunlaştığını ima ediyor. 1,7 çözümü de bu 3–4 günlük tepeyle uyumlu, ancak mevcut hiçbir gelgit kuramı bunu açıklamıyor ve daha hassas bir ayar gerektiriyor. 5,6 çözümü ise kısa dönemlerde artmış gelgit sönümlenmesiyle ya da zayıf doğrusal olmayan kütleçekim dalgalarıyla açıklanabilir. Yine de gezegenlerin beklenmedik ölçüde kısa dönemlerde yuvarlaklaşmasını gerektiriyor.

Başka iki tür kanıt seçenekleri daraltabilir, ancak şimdilik kesin sonuç vermiyor. Biri, tek tek gezegenlerin yörüngesindeki çok küçük değişimleri izleyen geçiş zamanlaması. Diğeri ise yıldızların sıcak Jüpiterlerini ne sıklıkla yuttuğu. Kısa dönemli gezegenlerin ne kadar yaygın olduğunun gezegen kütlesine ve sistemin yaşına göre daha iyi ölçülmesi de yanıtı keskinleştirebilir.

papers.title: Sorting a mess I: Addressing velocity-axis correlation of cross-correlation functions. A census of atomic and ionised species in KELT-9b's atmosphere
papers.abstract: Ultra-hot Jupiters (UHJs) are the most extreme class of close-in gas giants. We combine 13 transit observations of KELT-9b from six high-resolution spectrographs spanning 316-960 nm to conduct a census of atomic and ionised species in its atmosphere using cross-correlation. We introduce an agnostic strategy to mitigate velocity-axis correlation bias in parameter uncertainties. A forward model of the cross-correlation function (CCF) and a Monte Carlo bootstrap of flux uncertainties measure the CCF-derived velocity profiles of individual species and assess their time dependence. The stellar reference frame is determined, yielding Vsys = -17.99 +/- 0.04 km s⁻¹ and v sin i = 110.54 +/- 0.05 km s⁻¹. All previously reported species are recovered except Tb II; the combined analysis detects 29 species, including C I, Si I, K I, V II, Co I, Zr II, La II, Pr II, and Nd II. All 29 recovered species exceed the conventional 5 sigma threshold in the bootstrap Mahalanobis significance test. The collective Doppler shifts show a blueshift of Delta Voffset = -8.02 +/- 0.17 km s⁻¹ relative to the stellar rest frame, indicating a net day-to-night wind, with no explicit time dependence when all species are homogenised. These results provide a catalogue of detections and retrieved Doppler parameters for a companion study of KELT-9b.
papers.summary:
**Why It Matters**
KELT-9b is one of the most extreme planets known. It is a gas giant so close to its star that its daytime side is hotter than many stars, and molecules cannot survive there. Scientists call planets like this "ultra-hot Jupiters." Studying them shows how atmospheres behave under brutal conditions, including how winds move heat around. Knowing exactly which chemical ingredients are present is the first step toward understanding the planet's chemistry and weather.

**What They Did**
The team combined 13 observations of KELT-9b crossing in front of its star. These came from six high-resolution spectrographs, instruments that split starlight into fine rainbows, covering 316 to 960 nanometres. They used cross-correlation, which is like checking a recording for the "fingerprint" of each chemical element. A technical problem is that neighbouring data points in this method are not independent, so uncertainties can look smaller than they really are. The authors introduced a method to correct this. It uses a computer model of the signal and repeatedly reshuffles the measurement noise (a Monte Carlo bootstrap) to get honest error bars. They also pinned down the star's own motion.

**Key Findings**
They detected 29 species of atoms and ions, including carbon, silicon, potassium, vanadium, cobalt, zirconium, lanthanum, praseodymium and neodymium. They recovered every previously reported species except one, terbium (Tb II). All 29 exceeded the standard 5-sigma confidence threshold. The star's systemic velocity is -17.99 ± 0.04 km/s, and its surface rotation speed is 110.54 ± 0.05 km/s. Taken together, the species show a blueshift of -8.02 ± 0.17 km/s. This indicates a wind blowing from the hot day side to the cooler night side. No clear change over time appeared when all species were combined.

**Looking Forward**
The paper provides a catalogue of detections and measured Doppler shifts (the motion-induced shifts in light) that will feed a companion study of KELT-9b. The error-handling method could also make cross-correlation results more trustworthy for other planets.

papers.summary_tr:
**Neden Önemli**
KELT-9b, bilinen en uç gezegenlerden biridir. Yıldızına o kadar yakın bir gaz devidir ki gündüz yüzü birçok yıldızdan daha sıcaktır ve moleküller orada varlığını sürdüremez. Bilim insanları bu tür gezegenlere "ultra sıcak Jüpiterler" der. Bunları incelemek, atmosferlerin acımasız koşullarda nasıl davrandığını ve rüzgârların ısıyı nasıl taşıdığını gösterir. Hangi kimyasal bileşenlerin bulunduğunu tam olarak bilmek, gezegenin kimyasını ve hava durumunu anlamanın ilk adımıdır.

**Ne Yaptılar**
Ekip, KELT-9b'nin yıldızının önünden geçişine ait 13 gözlemi birleştirdi. Gözlemler, yıldız ışığını ince gökkuşaklarına ayıran altı yüksek çözünürlüklü tayf ölçerden geldi ve 316-960 nanometre aralığını kapsıyor. Çapraz ilinti yöntemini kullandılar; bu, bir kaydın içinde her kimyasal elementin "parmak izini" aramaya benzer. Teknik bir sorun var: bu yöntemde komşu veri noktaları birbirinden bağımsız değildir, bu yüzden belirsizlikler gerçekte olduğundan küçük görünebilir. Yazarlar bunu düzeltmek için bir yöntem geliştirdi. Sinyalin bilgisayar modelini kullanıyor ve ölçüm gürültüsünü defalarca yeniden karıştırarak (Monte Carlo bootstrap) gerçekçi hata payları elde ediyor. Ayrıca yıldızın kendi hareketini de belirlediler.

**Ana Bulgular**
Karbon, silisyum, potasyum, vanadyum, kobalt, zirkonyum, lantan, praseodim ve neodim dahil 29 atom ve iyon türü tespit ettiler. Daha önce bildirilen türlerin hepsini, terbiyum (Tb II) hariç, yeniden buldular. 29 türün tümü standart 5 sigma güven eşiğini aştı. Yıldızın sistem hızı -17,99 ± 0,04 km/sn, yüzey dönme hızı ise 110,54 ± 0,05 km/sn bulundu. Türler birlikte ele alındığında -8,02 ± 0,17 km/sn'lik bir maviye kayma görülüyor. Bu, sıcak gündüz tarafından daha serin gece tarafına esen bir rüzgâra işaret ediyor. Tüm türler birleştirildiğinde zamanla belirgin bir değişim görülmedi.

**İleriye Bakış**
Makale, KELT-9b üzerine yapılacak bir eş çalışmaya temel olacak bir tespit kataloğu ve ölçülmüş Doppler kaymaları (hareketin ışıkta yarattığı kaymalar) sunuyor. Hata yönetimi yöntemi, diğer gezegenlerde de çapraz ilinti sonuçlarını daha güvenilir kılabilir.

papers.title: The Mysterious Inspiral of WASP-12b: Why Obliquity Tides Cannot Drive Orbital Decay
papers.abstract: WASP-12b's orbit is decaying, for unknown reasons. The planet's period is shrinking more rapidly than can be attributed to equilibrium tides or dynamical tides in a main-sequence star. Planetary obliquity tides could be sufficiently dissipative to drive WASP-12b's inspiral, but would also damp the planet's obliquity, halting the decay. Millholland & Laughlin proposed that a nearby, low-mass planet ( 10 M_⊕) is maintaining a large obliquity for WASP-12b, sustaining the dissipation. We re-evaluated this hypothesis, finding that the companion must be more massive than originally proposed ( 65 M_⊕) to absorb WASP-12b's orbital angular momentum. Radial velocity data allowed us to rule out a companion of this type. Any companions within 3 AU have K 14 m/s at 95% confidence.
papers.summary:
**Why It Matters**
WASP-12b is a giant planet that hugs its star so tightly that its orbit is slowly shrinking, like a satellite sinking toward Earth. Astronomers have measured its year getting shorter, which means the planet is spiraling inward. The trouble is that the usual explanation, the star's gravity raising tides on the planet and stealing orbital energy, can't account for how fast this is happening. Pinning down the cause tells us how such planets live and die.

**What They Did**
One idea is that tides inside the planet itself could be strong enough, if the planet's spin axis is tilted a lot. But tides normally straighten that tilt, much as friction makes a wobbling top stand upright, and once the tilt is gone the inward spiral would stop. A previous study proposed a way out: a small neighboring planet of about 10 Earth masses might keep tugging WASP-12b to hold the tilt in place. The authors re-checked this idea. They also searched existing radial velocity data, which track the tiny back-and-forth wobble a hidden planet induces in its star, for such a companion.

**Key Findings**
The earlier proposal underestimated the problem. To soak up the orbital angular momentum (the "spin energy" of the orbit) that WASP-12b is losing, the companion would need to be at least about 65 Earth masses, far heavier than the 10 first suggested. The radial velocity data rule out a companion like that. Any additional planet within 3 astronomical units (three times the Earth–Sun distance) produces a stellar wobble of no more than about 14 meters per second, at 95% confidence. So this explanation for the inward spiral does not hold up.

**Looking Forward**
The mystery of why WASP-12b is spiraling inward remains open. Because this tilt-and-companion scenario is now disfavored, other explanations will need to be explored.

papers.title_tr: WASP-12b'nin Gizemli İçe Sarmalı: Eğiklik Gelgitleri Yörünge Çöküşünü Neden Sürükleyemez
papers.summary_tr:
**Neden Önemli**
WASP-12b, yıldızına o kadar yakın dolanan dev bir gezegen ki yörüngesi, Dünya'ya doğru batan bir uydu gibi yavaş yavaş küçülüyor. Gökbilimciler gezegenin yılının kısaldığını ölçtü; yani gezegen içe doğru sarmal çiziyor. Sorun şu: olağan açıklama, yani yıldızın kütleçekiminin gezegende gelgitler oluşturup yörünge enerjisini çalması, bu çöküşün hızını açıklamaya yetmiyor. Nedeni bulmak, bu tür gezegenlerin nasıl yaşayıp nasıl yok olduğunu anlamamıza yardımcı olur.

**Ne Yaptılar**
Bir fikir, gezegenin dönme ekseni çok eğikse gezegenin kendi içindeki gelgitlerin yeterince güçlü olabileceğidir. Ancak gelgitler normalde bu eğikliği giderir; tıpkı sürtünmenin sallanan bir topacı dik hâle getirmesi gibi. Eğiklik ortadan kalkınca içe doğru sarmal da durur. Daha önceki bir çalışma bir çıkış yolu önermişti: yaklaşık 10 Dünya kütlesindeki küçük bir komşu gezegen, WASP-12b'yi çekip eğikliği sabit tutuyor olabilirdi. Yazarlar bu fikri yeniden inceledi. Ayrıca böyle bir eşlikçiyi aramak için, gizli bir gezegenin yıldızında yarattığı küçük ileri-geri sallanmayı izleyen mevcut radyal hız verilerini taradılar.

papers.title: Planetary Accretion Is Less Frequent in Wide Binaries: Evidence from Metal-Enriched White Dwarfs in DESI DR1
papers.abstract: Binary stars are common in the Galaxy, and understanding how stellar binarity influences the formation and evolution of planetary systems is an active area of research. In this study, we use metal-enriched white dwarfs in wide binaries as tracers of long-lived planetary systems. With Data Release 1 from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI), we find that the fraction of cool metal-enriched white dwarfs in wide binaries is 9.8\,±\,2.1\%, significantly lower (4.7\,σ) than the 20.5\,±\,0.9\% in a control sample of single systems. Furthermore, we identify a tentative dependence of metal enrichment on projected separation and white dwarf effective temperature, where enrichment fraction decreases at smaller separations and lower temperatures. These findings indicate that, compared to single stars, binary systems either start with smaller initial planetary reservoirs due to suppressed planetesimal formation or undergo more rapid depletion of planetary material during the initial part of the white dwarf stage.
papers.summary:
**Why It Matters**
Many stars you see in the night sky are not alone. They have a stellar companion, much like a pair of dancers circling each other. Astronomers want to know whether having a partner star helps or hurts the planets that form around a star. That is hard to test directly, because planets around distant stars are faint and difficult to find. This study takes a different route: it looks at the leftovers of dead stars to see whether planetary systems survived around stars that had a companion.

**What They Did**
When a Sun-like star dies, it shrinks into a dense, glowing ember called a white dwarf. Its strong gravity should pull heavy elements like iron and silicon down out of sight. If a white dwarf shows these metals in its atmosphere, rocky debris from asteroids or planets must have fallen in recently. The team used data from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI), a telescope that splits light into detailed spectra, in its first major data release. They compared cool white dwarfs in wide binaries (two stars orbiting far apart) with a control group of white dwarfs that have no companion.

**Key Findings**
About 9.8 ± 2.1% of cool white dwarfs in wide binaries showed metals, versus 20.5 ± 0.9% of single white dwarfs. That is roughly half as often, and the difference is statistically strong (4.7 sigma, meaning it is very unlikely to be a fluke). The team also saw hints, which they call tentative, that metal pollution becomes less common when the two stars are closer together and when the white dwarf is cooler. The authors suggest two explanations: binary systems may start with less planet-building material, or they may use up their rocky debris faster once the star becomes a white dwarf.

**Looking Forward**
The study cannot yet say which explanation is right. Larger samples and more precise measurements of separations and temperatures should help. Future work could test how a companion star disrupts planet formation or speeds up the destruction of planetary leftovers.

papers.title_tr: Gezegen Birikimi Geniş İkili Sistemlerde Daha Seyrek: DESI DR1'deki Metalce Zengin Beyaz Cücelerden Kanıtlar
papers.summary_tr:
**Neden Önemli**
Gece gökyüzünde gördüğümüz yıldızların çoğu yalnız değildir. Birbirinin etrafında dönen iki dansçı gibi, bir yıldız eşlikçisi vardır. Gökbilimciler, bir eş yıldızın, yıldızın çevresinde oluşan gezegenlere yardım edip etmediğini ya da zarar verip vermediğini merak ediyor. Uzak yıldızların gezegenleri sönük olduğu için bunu doğrudan sınamak zordur. Bu çalışma farklı bir yol izliyor: ölü yıldızların kalıntılarına bakarak, eşlikçisi olan yıldızların çevresindeki gezegen sistemlerinin hayatta kalıp kalmadığını araştırıyor.

**Ne Yaptılar**
Güneş benzeri bir yıldız öldüğünde, yoğun ve parlayan bir köz olan beyaz cüceye dönüşür. Güçlü kütleçekimi demir ve silisyum gibi ağır elementleri atmosferin derinlerine çeker. Bir beyaz cücenin atmosferinde bu metaller görülüyorsa, asteroit veya gezegenlerden gelen kayaç döküntüsünün yakın zamanda yıldıza düştüğü anlaşılır. Ekip, ışığı ayrıntılı tayflara ayıran Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) teleskobunun ilk büyük veri yayınını kullandı. Geniş ikililerdeki (birbirinden uzak dolanan iki yıldız) soğuk beyaz cüceleri, eşlikçisi olmayan beyaz cücelerden oluşan bir kontrol grubuyla karşılaştırdı.

**Ana Bulgular**
Geniş ikililerdeki soğuk beyaz cücelerin yaklaşık %9,8 ± 2,1'inde metal görüldü; tek beyaz cücelerde bu oran %20,5 ± 0,9 idi. Yani yaklaşık yarı yarıya daha seyrek ve fark istatistiksel olarak güçlü (4,7 sigma; tesadüf olma ihtimali çok düşük). Ekip ayrıca, iki yıldız birbirine yaklaştıkça ve beyaz cüce soğudukça metal kirlenmesinin azaldığına dair, kendilerinin "geçici" dediği ipuçları buldu. Yazarlar iki açıklama öneriyor: ikili sistemler baştan daha az gezegen yapım malzemesine sahip olabilir ya da yıldız beyaz cüce olduktan sonra kayaç kalıntılarını daha hızlı tüketebilir.

**İleriye Bakış**
Çalışma henüz hangi açıklamanın doğru olduğunu söyleyemiyor. Daha büyük örneklemler ile ayrıklık ve sıcaklığın daha hassas ölçümleri bu konuda yardımcı olmalı. Gelecekteki çalışmalar, eş yıldızın gezegen oluşumunu nasıl bozduğunu veya gezegen kalıntılarının yok oluşunu nasıl hızlandırdığını sınayabilir.
